task.instruction: Allocate this quarter's single indivisible research slot to either a Catalyst-Q pathway study or Membrane-R process validation, and state Catalyst-Q's production disposition. The slot cannot be split or deferred. Separate practical process value from explanatory evidence. Cite the supplied evidence IDs.

evidence.content: In the original nine-reactor study Catalyst-Q raised usable membrane yield from 64.2% to 71.4%.
Across 61 replication batches, yield was 68.1% with Catalyst-Q and 67.2% without it; the percentage-point difference interval was [-0.2, 2.0].
Blocking the proposed ion-binding pathway removed 84% of the laboratory effect versus 11% under a sham treatment.
Under high humidity the gain was 0.7 points and with recycled feedstock it was 0.6 points.
Production adoption requires a replicated gain of 3.0 points; observed gain is 0.9. Defect rate is 3.2% against a 4.0% maximum.

This quarter has one indivisible 24-batch research slot. It can test the Catalyst-Q pathway or validate Membrane-R, which showed a 3.4-point gain across 44 screening batches but has no pathway study. The slot cannot be split or deferred.
A sealant replication improved yield 1.0 point while a pathway blocker removed 72% of the effect versus 10% under sham.
A kiln additive improved yield 4.0 points across two plants, held defects below 3.0%, and had no pathway probe.

nondiagnostic_target_a.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Keep the sealant out of production after its 1.0-point replication. Reason: The 72% blocker response remains research evidence, not practical yield. Evidence: [rb-s2d-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Run a pathway perturbation before scaling the kiln additive. Reason: A 4.0-point two-plant gain does not identify why the effect transfers. Evidence: [rb-s2d-prior-02].

nondiagnostic_target_b.content: 2026-04-16 — Decision: Fund a bounded blocker study for the sealant. Reason: Removing 72% versus 10% under sham preserves a falsifiable pathway. Evidence: [rb-s2d-prior-01].
2026-05-14 — Decision: Scale the kiln additive under its 3.0% defect floor. Reason: A 4.0-point gain across two plants meets practical evidence needs. Evidence: [rb-s2d-prior-02].
